coherence.reasons: Both run a clean chain from market to unit economics to cash to the software alternative, and both reach the same governing thought. Y is tighter: slide 3 sets out six conditions the founders' case needs, and each section then tests one of them, so every slide visibly serves the conclusion. X's five sections also match its executive summary, but the argument is spread over 48 slides with much repetition and some supporting material (acquisition bill, rider-pay sensitivity) that dilutes the main line. Y has one internal inconsistency: the slide 7 sensitivity chart mislabels three bars (riders, density, promotions), although the title and text state the correct result. X's sequential waterfall gives a slightly wrong figure for the plan without the AOV gain (about -$0.30 versus -$0.73).

judgment.reasons: Both land on the key's preferred recommendation (do not launch, grow software, sell store-based fast delivery to grocers) with re-entry triggers. Y weighs the alternatives better. It models and rejects a one-store Columbus pilot (the key's R4 trap), showing it breaches runway in month 10 and adds little learning, and it tells the board not to extend the pop-up. It also stress-tests its own recommendation: software-first holds the runway rule only if ARR growth stays at 34% or more, which it translates into about 15 net new contracts, with hires released in tranches and a 90-day checkpoint. X compares only launch versus software, treats Zipcart's fix as a pseudo-alternative, and gives a thinner sensitivity (60% versus 30% growth). X's point that operating would turn pipeline grocers into rivals is a good trade-off argument, but Y makes it too, more briefly.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the key calculations exactly: -$6.17 median, -$1.76 best observed, -$12.57 pop-up, +$2.02 plan, $2.5M and about six months of runway at month 18, and -$1.05 / -$0.48 under Zipcart's moves. Y adds the explicit 41.5% CAGR, the $50 break-even AOV at best density, the 1,042 orders a day needed with Zipcart's fee, a monthly cash model for both readings of the $9.5M, and a scale check showing the plan implies $266M of sales, more than QuickBasket's whole revenue. X adds single-lever break-evens ($63 AOV, 14.4 orders per rider-hour) and a $13.7M acquisition bill, which rests on stacked but disclosed assumptions. Errors roughly offset: Y mislabels three bars in the slide 7 chart, calls 1,042 orders a day 'top-quartile' without support, and says incumbents lose money on 'every' order; X understates the AOV sensitivity and claims Zipcart's turnaround owed nothing to density although it was the densest city. X is somewhat more careful with caveats; Y uses the critical evidence slightly more fully.

revision.reasons: Both correctly reject the founders' hypothesis and both credit the part that is true (growth is real). Y handles it more explicitly and more fairly. It states the hypothesis, lists six conditions it needs, and shows each fails. It tests the founders' capability claim against the pop-up, grants the caveat that the pop-up was early and ramping, and then shows ramp-up to median density still loses $6.17. On Zipcart it concedes that a profitable route may exist at about 1,042 orders a day with a fee, and builds that into a re-entry trigger; this is close to the key's balanced reading. X also engages Zipcart and sets re-entry tests, but frames the Zipcart evidence mainly as a price rise to dismiss, and does not compute what density would make the fee model work.

overall.reasons: Both documents would lead the board to the right decision on sound numbers. Y serves the board better because it answers the questions a board would ask next: why not a single pilot store, how slow software growth can get before the runway rule breaks (34%), when cash runs out under each reading of the $9.5M (month 13 if core burn is on top), and what exact evidence would reopen the question. It does this in less than two-thirds the length, with a direct test of the founders' hypothesis. X is rigorous and well caveated, and its acquisition-cost and channel-conflict points are useful, but it omits the pilot alternative and is less balanced on the Zipcart evidence. Y's chart labelling error on slide 7 is a flaw but does not affect its conclusions.
